q: Trade between two countries is called
e: Trade between countries is foreign trade.

q: A document sent by a seller listing goods and amounts due is an
e: An invoice lists the goods supplied and the amount due.

q: Which insurance principle requires full disclosure of facts?
e: Utmost good faith means full disclosure of material facts.

q: The bank that issues currency in Nigeria is the
e: The Central Bank of Nigeria issues the currency.

q: Who buys in bulk from manufacturers and sells to retailers?
e: Wholesalers buy in bulk and sell to retailers.

q: A business owned and run by one person is a
e: A sole proprietor owns and runs the business alone.

q: Which of these is a source of long-term finance?
e: Debentures are long-term loans to a company.

q: Goods held for sale in a shop are called
e: Stock is goods kept for sale.

q: The cheapest way to move bulky goods over long distances is by
e: Water transport is cheapest for bulky, non-urgent goods.

q: The main aim of advertising is to
e: Advertising informs and persuades buyers.

q: A cheque is an instrument of
e: A cheque is an order to a bank to pay money.

q: Shares are bought and sold on the
e: Shares are traded on the stock exchange.

q: Retail trade is the selling of goods
e: Retailers sell directly to final consumers.

q: A wholesaler
o: buys in bulk and sells to retailers
e: Wholesalers link producers and retailers.

q: The usual chain of distribution is
e: Goods normally pass from manufacturer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer.

q: A sole proprietorship is a business owned by
e: One person owns and usually runs it.

q: Limited liability means shareholders' loss is limited to
o: the amount unpaid on their shares
e: Shareholders cannot lose more than they invested.

q: Shares of a public limited company are traded on the
e: Public companies can list shares on the stock exchange.

q: A guiding principle of co-operative societies is
e: Each member has one vote regardless of shares held.

q: A document sent by a buyer asking a seller to supply goods is a
e: The buyer sends an order for the goods wanted.

q: A credit note is issued when
o: goods are returned or the buyer was overcharged
e: It reduces the amount the buyer owes.

q: A receipt is
e: A receipt proves payment was made.

q: A bill of lading is issued by the
o: carrier, acknowledging goods loaded for shipment
e: It is a receipt and contract of carriage for goods being shipped.

q: The right to insure something arises from having
e: You can only insure what you would suffer a loss from.

q: A premium is
o: the payment made to an insurer for cover
money paid out on a claim
e: The insured pays premiums to the insurer.

q: The principle of indemnity means the insured is
o: restored to the position before the loss
e: Insurance compensates for loss but should not give a profit.

q: A crossed cheque
o: can be cashed over the counter
must be paid into a bank account
e: Crossing makes the cheque payable only through a bank account.

q: An overdraft allows a customer to
o: withdraw more than the account balance
e: Banks may allow current account holders to go overdrawn.

q: A current account is mainly operated by
e: Current accounts are operated by cheques and are meant for frequent transactions.

q: The fastest means of transport is
e: Air transport is the fastest.

q: The main purpose of advertising is to
e: Advertising informs customers and persuades them to buy.

q: A tariff is a
e: Tariffs are duties placed on imported goods.

q: An embargo is a
o: ban on trade with a country
e: An embargo officially bans trade.

q: Entrepôt trade is
o: importing goods in order to re-export them
e: Goods are imported and then re-exported.

q: The stock exchange is a market for
o: buying and selling shares and bonds
e: It trades securities such as shares and bonds.

q: A dividend is
o: a share of profit paid to shareholders
e: Companies pay dividends out of profit.

q: A debenture is
o: a loan to a company with fixed interest
e: Debenture holders are creditors, not owners.

q: The Nigerian agency that regulates food and drugs is
e: NAFDAC is the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control.

q: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) is mainly concerned with
e: SON sets standards for goods.

q: A trade association is a
o: group of firms or traders with common interests
e: Traders form associations to protect shared interests.

q: Warehousing helps trade mainly by
o: storing goods until they are needed
e: Warehouses store goods and so bridge the gap between production and sale.

q: A trader buys goods for N80,000 and adds a mark-up of 25% on cost. The selling price is
e: 25% of 80,000 is 20,000, so selling price is 100,000.

q: A retailer gives 10% trade discount on goods listed at N20,000. The amount payable is
e: 10% of 20,000 is 2,000, so the buyer pays 18,000.

q: Sales are N500,000 and returns inwards are N20,000. The net turnover is
e: Net turnover equals sales less returns inwards: 480,000.

q: A building worth N5m is insured fully for N5m and a fire causes N2m damage. Under indemnity the insurer pays
e: Indemnity restores the actual loss only, which is N2m.

q: A trader has sales of N300,000 and cost of goods sold of N220,000. The gross profit is
e: Gross profit equals sales less cost of goods sold: 80,000.

q: Cost of goods sold is N600,000 and average stock is N100,000. The rate of stock turnover is
e: Rate of stock turnover is cost of goods sold divided by average stock: 6 times.

q: Goods cost N60,000 and sell for N75,000. The mark-up on cost is
e: Profit 15,000 divided by cost 60,000 is 25%.

q: A property worth N10m is insured for N5m under an average clause and suffers a N4m partial loss. The insurer pays
e: Payment is 5/10 of 4m, which is N2m.

q: The first step of the chain of distribution in the home trade is usually the
e: Goods originate with the producer or manufacturer.

q: The practice of one insurer passing part of a risk to another insurer is
e: Reinsurance spreads a large risk by ceding part to another insurer.

q: The principle that an insurer who pays a claim takes over the insured's rights against a third party is
e: Subrogation lets the insurer recover from the party responsible for the loss.

q: In a partnership, a partner who contributes capital but takes no part in management is a
e: A sleeping (dormant) partner invests but does not take part in running the business.

q: The document that sets out the rules governing the internal affairs of a company is the
e: Articles of Association regulate internal management of the company.

q: The document that states a company's objects and relationship with outsiders is the
e: The Memorandum defines the company's name, objects and capital.

q: A document inviting the public to buy shares in a company is a
e: A prospectus invites the public to subscribe for shares or debentures.

q: Which of these is a feature of a public enterprise?
e: Public enterprises are owned or controlled by government.

q: The process of transferring government-owned enterprises to private ownership is
e: Privatisation moves ownership from the state to private investors.

q: Bank notes in Nigeria are legal tender because they are
e: Legal tender must be accepted by law in settlement of debts.

q: The bank that holds the reserves of commercial banks and acts as lender of last resort is the
e: The central bank lends to banks in distress as lender of last resort.

q: A money order and postal order are services of the
e: The postal service provides these money transfer instruments.

q: A cheque returned unpaid because the drawer's account has insufficient funds is said to be
e: A cheque refused by the bank is dishonoured.

q: Which of these is a disadvantage of road transport?
e: Road transport suffers from frequent accidents compared with other modes.

q: The document prepared by an air carrier acknowledging receipt of goods for air transport is the
e: An air waybill is the consignment document for air freight.

q: The advertising medium that combines sight, sound and motion is
e: Television uses visual, audio and movement together.

q: Persuading a customer to buy by explaining a product's benefits is known as
e: Personal selling is direct face-to-face persuasion by a salesman.

q: Which of these is a function of the Nigerian Stock Exchange?
o: Providing a market for existing securities
e: It provides a secondary market for trading existing shares and bonds.

q: Consumer protection is mainly aimed at
e: Consumer protection shields buyers from fraud, poor quality and unsafe goods.

q: The organisation that regulates the export of Nigerian goods through promotion is the
e: NEPC promotes non-oil exports.

q: The regional body that promotes economic integration among West African states is
e: ECOWAS aims at free movement and trade among West African members.

q: The international organisation that lends to member countries with balance of payments problems is the
e: The IMF provides short-term balance-of-payments support.
